problem: Existing LLM-based zero-shot VLN agents use a single LLM as a black box; they show weak spatial reasoning and endpoint recognition, and their topological maps grow without bound, overloading the context on long-horizon (>10-13 step) tasks.
motivation: Long-distance R2R episodes and ambiguous endpoints (e.g. stopping in a hallway instead of the kitchen) are where zero-shot LLM navigators fail. Unbounded map or memory accumulation hurts LLM judgment and inflates cost, so a compact task-relevant memory plus explicit spatial reasoning about the destination should help.
key_idea: Combine a dynamically pruned topological map memory, an LLM spatial module (a fine-tuned Qwen-Sp that extracts objects and infers the destination layout, plus YOLO-World visual enhancement), and a GPT-4o decision module for zero-shot VLN.
insight: Each module contributes on R2R-ZS: removing Memory drops OSR from 63.9 to 58.8, removing Spatial drops SR from 50.9 to 47.7, and removing Viewpoint Selection drops SR to 49.5. The Spatial Module is pluggable: adding it to NavGPT raises SR from 36.1 to 38.9 and to MapGPT from 45.8 to 48.1. Pruning helps most on long tasks (25 long cases: SR 44.0 vs 24.0 for MapGPT), and it keeps prompt growth bounded.
method: Memory Module: builds a topological graph and, after t_start, prunes N_remove nodes. Candidates must be non-current, visited and temporally stale; they are ranked by P = λt·staleness + λd·(-degree) + λf·(-unexplored neighbors) + λdist·graph distance. The map is rendered as trajectory, map and supplementary text prompts.

I-O-S dataset: 28,414 (instruction, object list, destination spatial layout) tuples (25,694 train / 2,720 test) built from oracle paths with simulator GT object annotations. An LLM proposes layouts from object bounding boxes and humans verify them.

Qwen-Sp: Qwen3-4B fine-tuned with two LoRA adapters, one for object extraction from instructions and one for destination spatial layout inference. For REVERIE, GPT-4o with prompts mimicking Qwen-Sp is used instead.
Visual Input Enhancement: selects the camera view with minimum L1 angular distance to the target direction and annotates it with YOLO-World detections of the extracted objects.
Decision Module: GPT-4o takes the instruction, memory context, spatial layout and prompt info (history, previous plan, action options) and outputs the next viewpoint or stop.
Map Efficiency (ME) metric: expert-node coverage multiplied by a map-size penalty, with α=0.25.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as decision maker; Qwen-Sp (Qwen3-4B + LoRA, fine-tuned) for spatial reasoning; YOLO-World detector (frozen)
setting.training_data: Qwen-Sp fine-tuned on 25,694 I-O-S samples; navigation itself is zero-shot with no training of the decision LLM
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views at the current viewpoint with navigable viewpoint candidates (Matterport3D), with YOLO-World annotations
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (move to a neighboring viewpoint or stop)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT object annotations only used to build the I-O-S training data)

results: On R2R-ZS, MSNav reaches SR 50.9 / SPL 42.6, beating the GPT-4o-reproduced MapGPT (45.8 / 37.6). On full R2R val-unseen it gets SR 46 / SPL 40 versus MapGPT 44 / 35, and on REVERIE-ZS SR 45.7 / SPL 32.8 versus MapGPT 41.4 / 28.4. Qwen-Sp beats GPT-4o on I-O-S object extraction (F1 0.316 vs 0.270, NDCG 0.388 vs 0.325).
limitations: Cost and latency are high: $0.10-0.14 and 3-5 minutes per sample. Gains on the full R2R val-unseen set are modest, and the reported results use small subsets (216 R2R and 140 REVERIE samples).
The I-O-S dataset is indoor-only, which limits generalization. On REVERIE the fine-tuned Qwen-Sp is not used, because of contamination concerns.
